title: Contagious
author: Jonah Berger
thesisParagraph: Ideas, products, and behaviors spread less because of luck or advertising muscle than because they give ordinary people reasons to pass them along. Six design levers, summarized as STEPPS, make sharing more likely by shaping status, memory, feeling, visibility, usefulness, and narrative transport.

signatureMoves: packages social transmission into crisp mechanisms and memorable acronyms
uses marketplace oddities, restaurant choices, and everyday sharing as evidence
keeps the prose brisk, curious, and lightly amused by human predictability
turns popularity into a testable feature of the message, not magic
opens with a vivid business or cultural case before naming the principle
avoidMoves: Avoid "The point is" as a paragraph hinge.
Avoid "the question is" as a setup crutch.
Avoid triadic abstract-noun lists such as clarity, courage, and resilience.
Do not make virality sound like luck plus enthusiasm.
Do not bury the STEPPS-style mechanism under marketing adjectives.
does not rely on mystical trend forecasting
does not treat social media platforms as the core mechanism

voiceSpecimens: The thing did not spread because everyone became generous at once.
It spread because the story made the sharer look useful.
teachingArc: The opening principle explains why people share things that improve how they look to others. The middle principles move from mental cues to emotional activation, then to public observability and useful information. The final principle wraps the prior mechanics inside narratives that carry a message without feeling like promotion.
forbiddenMoves: Do not promise that attention alone creates persuasion.
Do not use social proof without naming what makes the thing shareable.
